findings.evidence: "Use repeated phrasing and escalation; preserve the rhythm and line breaks" and "Use a fenced block for spacing-sensitive ASCII" repeat familiar genre and Markdown conventions rather than adding expert knowledge. The main workflow is substantially more information-dense.
findings.fix: Remove the stock copypasta-composition sentence and generic ASCII-formatting explanation. Retain the sensitive-details guard and the concrete rule for preserving literal greentext prefixes.

findings.evidence: `tokens = re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", context.lower())` recognizes only straight apostrophes. Following the branch for "tests haven’t passed yet" produces tokens ["tests", "haven", "t", "passed", "yet"], misses the negation, and returns "success". This contradicts the documented neutral handling of negated outcomes, although the workflow separately cautions that suggestions are only hints.
findings.fix: Normalize typographic apostrophes to ASCII before tokenization so contractions match NEGATIONS. Add regression tests asserting `fry` for "tests haven’t passed yet", "the build didn’t fail", and "the deploy isn’t working"; retain the explicit user-confirmation requirement for success memes.
